title: Estimating the autumn flow slope cut March log-flow forecast error by 41% with a time trend at three Arctic gauges in 1981-2011
abstract: We tested whether an estimated autumn flow slope improves March flow forecasts at Ob, Lena and Yenisey gauges. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 and earlier-year fits for 30 common certified winters in 1981-2011. With a time trend in both models, the estimated slope cut equal-river mean squared log-flow error by 40.81% against a slope fixed at one. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was 24.97% to 49.99%. Last-25-winter fits gave 39.46%. The gain over a trend-only model was 10.49%, with limits of -1.94% to 21.99%. Without a trend, the gain was -4.77% and uncertain. Thus, the main gain depends on the model for temporal change and does not prove useful autumn information beyond time. Revised data, regulation, selected certified years and conditional uncertainty limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, an arithmetic audit and a figure support reproduction. Source records stay external.

display.caption: Mean reduction in squared log-flow forecast error. Intervals condition on the saved forecasts and use paired three-year blocks. The gain depends on the time trend and reference model.
